provenance.inputs_seen_by_extractor: this evaluation's body text only (no paper, no model output)
provenance.post_check: reviewer-name tokens replaced by [name] after the quote check

issues.text: The sample of 170 usable respondents (after dropping about 500 contacted and 301 completing, then exclusions) is small, and the evaluator thinks it may be too small to detect true effects; the paper itself acknowledges this in several places.
issues.quote: Such sample sizes may not be large enough to detect true effects, which was pointed out in various places throughout the article.

issues.text: The sample is designed to match Flemish gender and age distributions but it is unclear whether it is representative on education and income, which are common sampling targets. With 51% of respondents having undergraduate or postgraduate education, the results may only hold for that group.
issues.quote: it is unclear if it is also representative along education and income lines.

issues.text: The open-ended contingent valuation question for marginal WTP is prone to hypothetical bias, has high cognitive load, and is not considered best practice in stated preference guidance, so the evaluator does not find the WTP estimates credible.
issues.quote: Open-ended questions like these are known to suffer from hypothetical bias, as mentioned throughout the research, and are not by themselves considered a best practice for stated preference studies

issues.text: The evaluator finds the point estimates themselves not credible, though they may still help show relative magnitudes.
issues.quote: Though these particular results are a useful starting point, I do not find them highly credible, but I do agree with the conclusion that it can help inform our understanding of relative magnitudes.

issues.text: The WTA results are very sensitive to sample trimming methods, indicating a lack of robustness in the central WTA findings.
issues.quote: the WTA results are very sensitive to the sample trimming methods

issues.text: The large gap between WTA and WTP (comparable to an extremely large endowment effect) is a major problem that a larger sample would not fix, and it undermines the welfare valuations.
issues.quote: the discrepancy between WTA and WTP (comparable to an extremely large endowment effect)

issues.text: The large discrepancy between median and mean values, reflecting skewed distributions, is a serious problem that more data would not resolve, making the mean-based headline figures unreliable.
issues.quote: the discrepancy between median and mean (i.e. the skewness of the distribution).

issues.text: The valuation relies on humans estimating the welfare of non-human animals rather than the animals themselves, which limits what the measures can capture; the evaluator suggests this is a fundamental limitation, and that valuations of ending existence differ from valuations of a life not worth living.
issues.quote: the results derive from humans' estimations of non-human animal life.

issues.text: The policy section on meat taxation and climate trade-offs is too simplistic for policymakers; it does not model competing realistic policies or their effects on animal welfare costs in aggregate.
issues.quote: are perhaps too simplistic for policymakers.

issues.text: The paper's claim that a carbon tax would not cause substitution is asserted for a flat tax without analysis, and the evaluator says a better approach would compare several feasible policies and their animal welfare effects.
issues.quote: A better approach would have been to highlight a few different competing policies, politically feasible from the perspective of the governing body, and calculate how those policies would have affected the animal welfare costs

issues.text: The headline claim (median animal welfare cost of chicken of about 10 euro/kg versus a much higher mean) rests on a single-country hypothetical survey with a small sample and is not credible as a point value, though it may inform non-zero lower bounds.
issues.quote: I do not find the point value itself credible.
